newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session firmer.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session firmer.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended modestly higher in light trading Monday, getting a lift late in the session from mixed trade buying and local short-covering, dealers said.
"The trade buying induced the ring to do some short covering," one trader said.

The market sagged in early going, following losses overnight in London, but manufacturer interest toward the lows prevented a test of support at $1,370 a tonne basis March and helped push prices above the unchanged mark, traders said.
March futures rose to a high of $1,386, partially filling a gap on the charts between $1,382 and $1,388, before upward momentum faded.

March futures ended at $1,384, up $8, having traded from $1,371 to $1,386. May rose $11, to $1,407. Spot December finished down $3, to $1,333. With three days to go before December's expiry, open interest on the contract was only 10 lots.
Technically, traders said $1,373-1,372 emerged as a solid support area, while nearby resistance was pegged at $1,388-1,395. The next key upside target was seen at $1,410.

With market participants beginning to focus on squaring their books ahead of the new year, some traders said they expected prices range narrowly between $1,350 and $1,400 through the month of December.

Reaction to fundamentals was muted, traders said. Ghana's cocoa purchases in the fifth week of the 1996/97 season ending November 14 were 22,432 tonnes compared with 28,178 in the corresponding week of the previous year.

In other news, General Cocoa in its weekly newsletter "guesstimated" Ivorian arrivals through Nov. 30 were around 290,000 tonnes compared with an estimated total of 410,000 tonnes at the same time last year.
Turnover was thin, reaching only 4,858 lots at the close.
